doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Meaning of 'easternal' and ritual in the poetry
summary: Grimes explains 'easternal' and an off-camera voice links it to returning to New York.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I look at your upcoming calendar. It looks pretty healthy to me. There’s words that I’ve noticed from both of you on your CDs and in your poetry book, that seem to occur pretty often: forces, aggregate and things about rituals and I love this word “easternal mysticism.” What are the rituals that you are referring to?
You’ll have to ask Henry about that.

Yeah, uh going east. Like it’s easternal when you go east. You know like that. The sun rises in the east or you know, impulses derive their existence coming from the east or like that. And because I was writing that I had something to do instead of watching TV, after work, I’d do that, I’d write after work, essentially that’s what it is. But yeah, I’m glad somebody heard my poetry. I didn’t expect that to happen.
Yeah. Isn’t that interesting. I hear you’ve got quite a collection too.
Yeah, I’ve got to do something, however you do that, you know, but I’m open for suggestions.
I think it was also a reference to coming back to New York, which he was predicting to himself and preparing himself for.
Coming back from the west coast to the east coast.

Yeah, that also, because that gives you the opportunity to come from some source and understanding. You know that’s a whole source right there, you know, if you’re going to return to music or return from music. You know it’s a lot of knowledge in that, I mean a lot of understanding and a lot of, nothing is something you can really take for granted but you know it’s there. All those things can really come together and make a metaphor and it becomes a metaphor. I mean it can, but you might do something else. I’m not saying do that, it might be something else.
